content: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) continues to be one of the primary causes of mortality in individuals with diabetes. Research studies, including ACCORD, ADVANCE, and VADT, have examined the impact of intensive glycemic control on cardiovascular outcomes. These studies demonstrated that while strict glucose management can effectively reduce complications like neuropathy, its effects on cardiovascular outcomes were inconsistent. It is crucial to adopt a personalized approach to glucose management in order to minimize potential risks and optimize cardiovascular benefits. Follow-up studies, such as ADVANCE-ON and ACCORDION, have further investigated the long-term effects of intensive glycemic control on cardiovascular disease outcomes. These studies found that although intensive glucose control can lower the occurrence of cardiovascular events, such as myocardial infarctions, it does not necessarily lead to a reduction in long-term mortality rates. Interestingly, the most pronounced cardiovascular benefits were observed in patients who transitioned back to conventional glucose management after undergoing a period of intensive glycemic control.
